Growth rates of each species at each site

Source: R/traits.R
growth_rates.Rd

Density-independent growth rate of species \(j\) at site \(i\), \(r_j \exp(-(E_i - \theta_j)^2 / (2 \sigma_j^2))\), with \(r_j\) = r_max, \(\theta_j\) = optimum and \(\sigma_j\) = sigma: a Gaussian response whose standard deviation is the niche breadth sigma. This sigma equals \(\sqrt{2}\) times the niche breadth parameter of Thompson et al. (2020).

Usage

growth_rates(env, traits)

Arguments

env

Environment of each site; for several axes, a matrix, data frame or list with one axis per column or element, in the order of traits.

traits

Data frame from species_traits(), or any data frame with columns optimum, sigma and r_max; for several axes, a list of them with the same species.

Value

Numeric matrix with one row per site and one column per species: the density-independent growth rate of each species at each site.

Details

With several environmental axes, each species has a response to each axis and the growth rate is the product of the responses, as in simulate_static(): a Gaussian niche in several dimensions whose axes are independent (no correlation between the responses to different axes), with the optimum and breadth of each axis in its own set of traits. The maxima multiply too, so give the traits of all but one axis r_max of 1, for example with species_traits(rmax_range = c(1, 1)).

See also

Other simulate metacommunities: as_metacommunity(), colonisation_history(), evolution_control(), logistic_gradients(), mc_dynamics(), simulate_evolving_metacommunity(), simulate_logistic(), simulate_metacommunity(), simulate_static(), speciation_control()

Examples

set.seed(1)
g <- growth_rates(seq(0, 100, 10), species_traits(3))
round(g, 2)
#>        sp1  sp2  sp3
#>  [1,] 3.13 0.00 7.61
#>  [2,] 3.94 0.00 0.00
#>  [3,] 4.28 0.00 0.00
#>  [4,] 4.00 0.00 0.00
#>  [5,] 3.23 0.00 0.00
#>  [6,] 2.25 0.01 0.00
#>  [7,] 1.35 0.07 0.00
#>  [8,] 0.70 0.52 0.00
#>  [9,] 0.31 2.15 0.00
#> [10,] 0.12 5.02 0.00
#> [11,] 0.04 6.66 0.00
